name: Random Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity
definition: For a fixed known probability distribution $\mu$ on the domain, assumed to give positive mass to every relevant disagreement set, the **Random Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity** is the least worst-case expected number of proper equivalence queries needed to identify a target in $\mathcal H$, when a failed hypothesis $h\in\mathcal H$ receives a counterexample sampled from $\mu$ conditioned on the disagreement set with the target. Thus the quantity is properly written $\mathrm Q_{\mathrm{rpeq}}(\mathcal H;\mu)$.
graph_summary: Expected proper-equivalence-query complexity under a fixed known counterexample distribution $\mu$.
comments: This is distribution-dependent rather than a pure invariant of $\mathcal H$.  No projection comparison is asserted until a convention for transporting $\mu$ through a projection is fixed.
origin_references: Introduced by Angluin and Dohrn in \cite{angluin2017random}.
